speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a neonate presenting with seizures and lethargy three days after birth; can you tell me if there is a history of maternal fever or chorioamnionitis during your pregnancy?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Sepsis secondary to Chorioamnionitis.

I note your low birth weight and history of maternal chorioamnionitis, which are major risk factors. Given your clinical presentation of seizures and lethargy, I must immediately evaluate for infection and metabolic derangements. REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, Blood Culture, and Serum Glucose/Calcium. REQUEST IMAGES: Cranial Ultrasound to rule out intraventricular hemorrhage.
